Dear Meadow Solutions,

Re: Plumbing request (toilet cistern continuously filling), Flat 14, 134 Copperfield Walk, Cedarford, ZZ4 4ZZ – ref R/PM031-1.

Thank you for your email of 27/07/2024. Unfortunately our system could not read its contents, so we can't see your update.

Could you please reply again in the body of the email (not only as an attachment) confirming:
- whether the visit booked for 26/07/2024 (2–5pm) took place;
- what you found and whether the cistern fault has been fixed;
- if further work is needed, your quote with photos and an estimated completion time (please don't proceed with quoted work until we confirm approval).

Kind regards,
Northbridge Lettings

data.reasoning:
That contractor email is hard to make out, and there's a slight date discrepancy between the visit and the call, plus some inconsistency in the company name used. I should hold off and ask the contractor directly to confirm the outcome of the visit, keeping each message to one person at a time — contractor first, possibly tenant separately about the cistern.

The cistern overflow is a minor water-wastage issue rather than an emergency, worth flagging alongside the leakage notice from the water company. I'll note the access arrangement that the tenant is fine with entry when away, and that there are two different contact numbers in play — one for the tenant, one for the provider. Time to send the contractor message.

result.summary: The contractor emailed after the visit booked for 26/07/2024, but the system couldn't read the email (events 015–016). So we don't know if the visit happened, if the toilet is fixed, or if a quote is needed. I've asked Meadow Solutions to send the update again in the email body. The ticket is on hold for 2 days, with a chase to follow if they don't reply. It doesn't need a person yet because the contractor can answer this themselves.

judgement.why_this_decision: Landlord approval was recorded (approval 28, event 003) and a visit was booked for 26/07/2024, 2–5pm (events 011–013). The only new thing is a contractor email (event 016) that the system couldn't read (event 015). Without its contents I can't move to closeout or ask the landlord to approve a quote. The contractor can answer directly, so asking them is the right next step.

alternatives_considered.why_not: The missing information can come from the contractor. Nothing conflicts, there's no safety risk and no cost is in dispute.
Nothing confirms the work was done.
Rule of one clear ask. The contractor is the primary source, and we can check with the tenant at follow-up if the contractor doesn't reply.
Without a hold the case would go quiet, and the contractor's update would stay unread.
